_comment: Town-level stance on a topic, set by hand from the records. stance: against | leaning_against | regulating | leaning_for | for | mixed | unclear | not_relevant. Towns not listed get an automatic call from keyword cues (see site.py). Reviewed 2026-11-03 (after full crawl).

Keene.basis: City Council referred a temporary moratorium on data centers and crypto mining to the Planning Board (Sep–Oct 2026).

Nottingham.basis: Warehouse data center proposal withdrawn after a 25,000-signature petition; 12-month moratorium passed 1,335–143 (Sep 2026).

Greenfield.basis: Planning Board proposed a moratorium on AI data centers to give itself a year to write an ordinance (Aug 2026).

Stratford.basis: Select Board drafting a warrant article to amend the land use ordinance to prohibit data centers (Sep–Oct 2026).

Canterbury.basis: Town meeting passed a zoning amendment banning data centers (Mar 2026); Select Board signed a letter opposing HB 639.

Hampton Falls.basis: Planning Board agreed a data center 'does not fit the look and feel' of the town and moved to say so in the Industrial section (Jun 2026).

Peterborough.basis: Planning Board raised data centers and crypto mining as a new zoning issue, citing severe concerns about power and water demand (Nov–Dec 2025).

Hooksett.basis: Planning Board asked 'do we want them or not?'; a member proposed a moratorium (Sep 2026). No vote yet.

Candia.basis: Zoning currently allows data centers by right; the Planning Board agreed to review an amendment removing that, though one member called them quiet neighbors (Sep–Oct 2026).

Warner.basis: Residents asked the Planning Board for an ordinance to keep data centers out (Sep–Nov 2026). The board hasn't acted.

Dalton.basis: Concern raised that Dalton, with no zoning ordinance, could be targeted for an unwanted AI data center (Sep 2026).

Bethlehem.basis: Select Board opposed HB 639; Planning Board drafted a crypto-mine ordinance modeled on Fitzwilliam's (2025). Found by web search.

Barrington.basis: Conservation Commission raised wetland concerns about the Nottingham proposal next to Barrington land (May 2026). Found by web search.

Franconia.basis: Conservation Commission objected to HB 639, which would limit local control over crypto-mining data centers (Jun 2026).

Bow.basis: Talks reported over a data center at the former Merrimack Station; residents packed the Sep 22 Select Board meeting to oppose it. Planning Board reviewing data center zoning amendments Nov 5, 2026.

Rochester.basis: Zoning amendment defines data centers and limits them to the Recycling Industrial District with a conditional use permit; residents largely opposed (Aug 2026). Found by web search.

Londonderry.basis: Planning Board asked staff to develop data center regulations, locating them in industrial districts (Sep 2026).

Derry.basis: Zoning ordinance adds a definition for 'Data Center or Information-Processing Facility' (effective Sep 2026).

Boscawen.basis: Site plan regulations add a new Section 3.12 for data centers and high-intensity computing (Nov 2026).

Bradford.basis: Planning Board drafted rules on water, noise, electric-rate impacts and coverage for data centers, then broadened them to all industrial uses (Aug–Sep 2026).

Chester.basis: Planning Board discussing zoning amendments to restrict bitcoin-mining data centers (2025–2026).

Newport.basis: Master Plan discussion agreed not to attempt a categorical prohibition and to address impacts instead (Aug 2026).

Tamworth.basis: Conservation Commission asked the Planning Board to research ordinance revisions for data centers (Jul 2026).

Swanzey.basis: Conservation Commission researching groundwater protections against large users such as data centers (Feb 2026).

Fremont.basis: Conservation Commission concerned about water use; joint work with the Planning Board planned for 2027 zoning (Aug 2026).

Claremont.basis: Planning Board discussing a working definition of data centers (Nov 2026).

Salem.basis: Planning Board looking at adopting a data center definition at a councilor's request (May 2026).

Durham.basis: Energy Committee working on definitions and the best regulatory approach, citing Nottingham (2026).

Strafford.basis: Board agreed data centers need addressing after Nottingham; currently possible by special exception (Jun–Jul 2026).

Windham.basis: No current prohibition; data centers fall under industrial. Board discussing treating them under the utilities definition (Sep 2026).

Hudson.basis: Proposed zoning amendment adds 'data center' to the allowable uses in the Industrial Zone, with a definition (Jan 2026).

Concord.basis: Site plan review for an 8,160 sq ft micro data center at 52 Locke Road in the Industrial district (Feb 2026).

Franklin.basis: At Council public comment, one resident asked for a citizen committee to study costs and benefits; another spoke in support of exploring data center development (Aug 2026).

Farmington.basis: Planning Board discussion; one member cautioned against overregulating what may be a passing trend (Jun 2026).

Newfields.basis: Planning Board asked whether a moratorium was needed; staff said the town is reasonably protected by existing rules (Sep 2026).

Littleton.basis: Zoning board reviewed research on pros and cons (Jul 2026). No position yet.

Allenstown.basis: Select Board received a resident letter about the Bow proposal and voted on a follow-up motion (Sep 2026).

Acworth.basis: Select Board asked whether the Planning Board should look at data centers proactively (Apr 2026).

Amherst.basis: Planning Board member asked to discuss a data center use (Sep 2026).

Barnstead.basis: Planning Board will discuss data centers at a future meeting (Sep 2026).

Bartlett.basis: Planning Board discussing whether the Master Plan should address allowing data centers and possible requirements (Sep–Oct 2026).

Bedford.basis: Resident questions about data centers at a Select Board meeting (Jun 2026).

Winchester.basis: Data centers listed as a possible warrant article topic for a work session (May–Jun 2026).

Laconia.basis: Conservation Commission gathering information on data centers and crypto mining (2025–2026).

Exeter.basis: Select Board packet includes NHMA's legislative bulletin opposing the state data center bill. Not a local proposal.

Hampton.basis: State senator's update on SB 439, a statewide data center zoning bill. Not a local proposal.

Stratham.basis: State senator's update on SB 439. Not a local proposal.

Sutton.basis: Select Board agenda lists NHMA's bulletin on data centers. Found by web search.

Goffstown.basis: Mentions are the town's own IT 'datacenter' equipment.

Nashua.basis: Mention is an IT closet relocation in a building contract.

Brookfield.basis: Mention is AI tools used to write minutes.

Wolfeboro.basis: Mention is the state's census 'Data Center' office.

Dover.basis: Planning document briefing on energy supply notes data centers as a new large load that may use small modular reactors in place of diesel backup, sited at former gas or coal plants. Informational, no proposal.

Pembroke.basis: Resident raised concerns at the Select Board about the proposed hyperscale data center in neighboring Bow: property values, taxes, noise, water and electric demand (Sep 2026).

Surry.basis: Zoning board flagged data centers, solar farms and windmills as uses needing definitions in its ordinance update (Aug 2026).

Salem.basis: Small modular reactors discussed as part of the 'Freedom and Prosperity' development proposal (Aug 2025).

Farmington.basis: SMRs mentioned as a possible future power source for data centers (Jun 2026).

Dover.basis: Planning document notes data centers may use SMRs as diesel-generator replacements at brownfield sites such as former gas or coal plants.
